audits.title: Achieving Door-to-Balloon Time ≤90 Minutes in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI): Results of a Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Door-to-balloon time ≤90 minutes in at least 90% of eligible patients
audits.setting: SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, tertiary care

cycle1.result: 564 of 620 (91.0%) achieved D2B ≤90 minutes, meeting the benchmark.

audits.other_findings: 56 (9.0%) delayed, mainly due to delayed consent (37.5%), medical stabilisation (32.1%) and diagnostic ambiguity (30.4%).
audits.citation: Krishnan R, Dhileeban CM, S H, P AU, Balaji S, Kavitha B. Achieving Door-to-Balloon Time ≤90 Minutes in ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI): Results of a Retrospective Audit. . 2025. doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-7559914/v1.

audits.title: Impact of an audit program and other factors on door-to-balloon times in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction patients destined for primary coronary intervention.
audits.setting: Cardiovascular Center and Emergency Department, Far Eastern Memorial Hospital

cycle1.result: Geometric mean door-to-balloon time 164.9 minutes; median 147.5 minutes.

audits.intervention: Audit programme collecting time data for essential intervals with feedback to Emergency Medicine and Cardiology departments.

cycle2.result: Geometric mean 141.9 minutes (p = 0.039); median 136.0 minutes (p = 0.09); adjusted reduction 35.5 minutes (p = 0.004).

audits.other_findings: Female sex (+58.4 minutes) and posterolateral infarction were associated with longer times; GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor use with shorter times.
audits.citation: Lai CL, Fan CM, Liao PC, Tsai KC, Yang CY, Chu SH, et al.. Impact of an audit program and other factors on door-to-balloon times in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction patients destined for primary coronary intervention. Acad Emerg Med. 2009;16(4):333-342. doi:10.1111/j.1553-2712.2009.00372.x. PMID: 19456296.

audits.title: Time to ECG diagnosis delays inter-hospital transfer to revascularization in STEMI patients presenting to a regional emergency department: a five-year audit.
audits.standard: Door-to-balloon time ≤120 min; door-to-ECG time ≤10 min
audits.setting: Connolly Hospital Blanchardstown emergency department, with transfer to Mater Misericordiae University Hospital

cycle1.result: Median door-to-balloon time 117.5 min (IQR 99.3-170.8); 52.5% met the ≤120 min target; median door-to-ECG 18.0 min (IQR 9.0-46.8), 28.8% met the ≤10 min target.

audits.other_findings: Time from ED arrival to diagnostic ECG was a major contributor to delay.
audits.citation: Shpigelman J, Proshkina A, Roman M, Maleady K, Casserly I, Blake G, et al.. Time to ECG diagnosis delays inter-hospital transfer to revascularization in STEMI patients presenting to a regional emergency department: a five-year audit. Ir J Med Sci. 2024;193(5):2203-2207. doi:10.1007/s11845-024-03705-6. PMID: 38748194.
